key_insight: Plasma p-tau217 was elevated in both Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), while the p-tau217/NfL ratio better distinguished the two diseases.
clinical_relevance: These findings support research into combined biomarkers rather than interpreting elevated p-tau217 alone as specific to AD.
method: Measured five plasma biomarkers in 551 participants across 10 diagnostic groups, including amyloid-PET-negative controls.
Compared biomarker levels and p-tau217-inferred amyloid positivity across groups.
Evaluated discrimination using ROC-AUC and tested clinical and longitudinal associations within ALS.
evidence_signal: The p-tau217/NfL ratio distinguished ALS from AD with an AUC of 0.92 (95% CI 0.85–0.97), versus 0.65 (0.52–0.76) for p-tau217 alone.
watch_item: The main comparisons were cross-sectional, amyloid positivity was inferred from p-tau217, and no ALS clinical or longitudinal association survived multiple-comparison correction.
paper_title: Plasma phosphorylated tau species across neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular diseases: An ONDRI study
